Two cohorts are dimensioned by simulation, each under two Bayesian criteria,
for two outcome variables. Every virtual study is calibrated with real data:
SWAN Visit-10 hormone assays, DKT-atlas cortical thickness, and the
laboratory's monitor-calibrated PM$_{2.5}$ model surface (2013--2022) mapped to
the cohort's residential comunas in Chile.

- **Cohort 1**: women aged 40--55 across the menopausal transition; in the
  exposure arm, adults with reconstructable long-term residential PM$_{2.5}$
  exposure.
- **Cohort 2**: adults aged 60--75 with Mild Cognitive Impairment (MCI)
  vs.\ cognitively healthy controls.

## Reports

### Hormonal arm (PC1 of FSH and estradiol)

[**Version 3: Bayesian-Lasso pipeline**](sample_size_report_v3.html)
Required $n$ under the laboratory's own analysis: a hierarchical Bayesian Lasso
regressing the hormonal PC1 on twenty brain principal components plus age;
success is at least one brain component whose 95% credible interval excludes
zero. Includes recovery of the posterior standardized $\beta$, sensitivity to
the number of components and to Bayes-factor thresholds, and Cohort 2.

[**Version 4: global-model Bayes factor (conditional MVG)**](sample_size_report_v4.html)
Required $N$ under a permutation-marginalized conditional multivariate Gaussian
generator: a global effect $R^2$ is split at random across components and
evidence is the Bayes factor of the full regression against the null
(equivalent to `BayesFactor::regressionBF`). Includes Cohort 2 with the
hormonal PC1 in the model.

### PM$_{2.5}$ exposure arm (residential model surface, 2013--2022)

[**Version 3 (PM$_{2.5}$): Bayesian-Lasso pipeline**](sample_size_report_v3_pm25.html)
The same laboratory criterion applied to the standardized residential
PM$_{2.5}$ exposure index (600 georeferenced participants, 52 comunas).

[**Version 4 (PM$_{2.5}$): global-model Bayes factor**](sample_size_report_v4_pm25.html)
The alignment-free global criterion applied to the exposure arm, with the
residential exposure included in the Cohort-2 model.

## Formats and reproducibility

Each report also exists as PDF and LaTeX in `reports/` of the repository, and
as Quarto source (`.qmd`) alongside these pages. The simulation engines, the
frozen calibration data and all numeric outputs live in `code/`, `data/` and
`results/`; every table in the reports is reproducible with fixed seeds. See
the repository `README.md` for commands.
